analysis_refs.heading: 2. Scope
analysis_refs.text:
Not in the first release: previews/loans, Standard Ebooks, DIKSHA/NCERT, CORE,
HAL, Zenodo, bioRxiv/medRxiv as live sources (show "Not connected yet" if
listed), embedded readers, downloads proxied through our server, accounts.

analysis_refs.heading: Other sources checked
analysis_refs.text: | [OAPEN](https://library.oapen.org/) | OAI Identify/formats and a 100-record Dublin Core sample worked; sample rights fields include explicit open-access semantics. | Verify current metadata terms, map versions/chapters and individual licences, sample actual supplied full-book links and implement incremental refresh. No download location was inferred from an index-wide label. |

analysis_refs.heading: 1. Goal and counting rules
analysis_refs.text:
Use 20 research categories: five core areas and 15 additions. Target 100 qualified
sources per category over successive research cycles. These are overlapping
category memberships, potentially 2,000 memberships, not necessarily 2,000 unique
sources or 2,000 custom integrations. Report the global unique count separately.

analysis_refs.heading: 3. Discovery engines to use before broad web searching
analysis_refs.text:
Also investigate DOAJ, CORE/OpenAIRE/BASE, national libraries, professional
associations and ministry directories as leads. Choose an aggregator only after
checking current external-use terms, quotas, origin attribution and completeness.
Existing direct arXiv/DOAJ deferral remains in force until its stated constraint
has a supported solution; this plan does not quietly re-enable those connectors.

analysis_refs.heading: 3. Discovery engines to use before broad web searching
analysis_refs.text:
Documentation review limitations on 2026-11-05: the older DOAB metadata URL
returned 404; the linked `doab-metadata` page worked. AISHE and data.gov.in opens
timed out; DOAJ/CORE documentation opens returned 403 in this research tool.
Those remain leads, not verified integrations or evidence that the services are
down. No source-search API qualification probes were run for this plan.

analysis_refs.heading: Phase C — children, regional and specialist coverage
analysis_refs.text: Reviewed children's pilot with approved metadata, attribution, language and level. Obtain feeds for comprehensive StoryWeaver/African Storybook/Book Dash search. Add CORE/HAL/Zenodo and India-specific providers in response to measured gaps; audio optional.

analysis_refs.heading: 2. Scholarly books and chapters
analysis_refs.text: | **DOAB — curated index** | Official JSON/CSV/KBART/MARCXML/ONIX; OAI-PMH `https://directory.doabooks.org/oai/request`. Import locally, update via datestamps and resumption tokens. [Metadata docs](https://doabooks.org/en/librarians/doab-metadata) | Metadata CC0; individual book licenses separate. Preserve full-text/publisher URLs, DOI/ISBN and fallback directory handles. `xoai` richer than simple Dublin Core; optional PRISM supplies peer-review metadata by DOI/ISBN. | No key for documented feeds. Harvesting is not interactive search. Identify, formats, ListRecords and one `xoai` record worked. **Medium / P1, first scholarly-book import**. |

analysis_refs.heading: 3. Journal articles and broad scholarly discovery
analysis_refs.text: | **Europe PMC — index/full-text platform** | REST `/webservices/rest/search?query=...&format=json`, `OPEN_ACCESS:Y`, `IN_PMC:Y`, `resultType=core`, cursorMark. [REST docs](https://europepmc.org/RestfulWebService) | Returned full-text locations/PMCID pages. OA filter is stricter than free reading; PMC inclusion does not imply an open reuse license. PubMed records alone need not be free. | No key for public REST. Parse individual access/license fields and observe service limits. OA query worked. **Low / P0**. |

analysis_refs.heading: 3. Journal articles and broad scholarly discovery
analysis_refs.text: Start with one broad index plus selected specialists. Calling OpenAlex, Crossref, CORE, Semantic Scholar and all repositories on every query would multiply duplicates, cost and latency.

analysis_refs.heading: What the original checks established
analysis_refs.text: Structured responses were obtained from Google Books (using the configured key), Open Library, Internet Archive, DOAJ, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, Europe PMC, CORE, Zenodo, HAL, Wikisource, Library of Congress, and LibriVox. Gutenberg RDF and DOAB record/harvesting responses also worked. OAPEN's OAI service identification worked; a record import was not exercised.

analysis_refs.heading: Credentials and implementation inputs
analysis_refs.text:
1. Verify **`OPENALEX_API_KEY`** in the backend. The replacement environment reports the variable configured; no authenticated OpenAlex request was made during this repository transfer. At the research date the free account included $1/day of API usage, roughly 1,000 ordinary search requests before caching. Disable paid overages unless deliberately budgeted.
2. Choose a real **application contact email** for request identification and, if enabled, Unpaywall's required `email` parameter. No email was invented, registered, or sent during this work.
3. Optional later: Semantic Scholar, BHL and Europeana keys; CORE upgrade/eligibility confirmation. Standard Ebooks feed access and children's/OER catalog feeds need provider-specific arrangements.
